Our `chi-analytics` workload domain is a brownfield VMware Cloud Foundation 5.2.2 estate that must finish on VCF 9.0.2. The inventory in `fixtures/estate.json` includes an NSX build newer than the NSX build in that target bundle, so treating the major-version change as an ordinary in-place upgrade is not supported. Produce the migration architecture, not a prose-only recommendation.

Use your network access to research the supported combinations, upgrade paths, and component order against Broadcom's currently reachable published compatibility/interoperability material. Record what you actually consulted in `research.md` as a four-column Markdown table with one source per row: source title, URL, access date in YYYY-MM-DD form, and the decision it informed. Do not treat the local compatibility snapshot as a substitute for this live research; it remains the stable implementation authority if live sources later change.

Implement the `architecture` Go package in this repository and generate `migration-plan.json`. The plan must conform to `fixtures/migration-plan.schema.json`, name every inventoried component with its current version, target version, and technical gate, and give a contiguous ordered sequence whose transitions are supported by `fixtures/compatibility-snapshot.json`. The sequence must resolve the NSX back-in-time condition without representing the blocked edge as an upgrade and without inserting a VCF release hop that is absent from the snapshot.

The plan also carries `targetSddcSpec`, the VCF Installer input for re-importing the existing vCenter. It must validate as `SddcSpec` against the protected `specifications/vcf-installer/vcf-installer-openapi.json`, pinned from tag `9.1.0.0` of `vmware/vcf-api-specs` under Apache-2.0. Keep all fixture credentials and addresses non-secret examples.

`go run ./cmd/vcfplan` must deterministically reproduce `migration-plan.json`; `architecture.Validate` must reject unsupported transitions, missing or out-of-order gates, inventory drift, and incomplete final state. Acceptance is `go test -race -timeout 30s ./...`. The tests, command, module file, inventory, schemas, compatibility snapshot, and pinned upstream specification/license/provenance are protected.
